questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the box.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is followed by a noun phrase (the heavy rain).

wrongReasons.although: 'although' is followed by a clause (subject + verb), not by a noun phrase like 'the heavy rain'.
wrongReasons.however: 'however' links two separate sentences. It is not followed by a noun phrase like this.
wrongReasons.because of: 'because of' gives a reason. The walk happened in spite of the rain, so we need 'despite'.

questions.text: ___ the heavy rain, we went for a walk.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the box.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if ... not': I won't go if you don't come.

wrongReasons.if: 'I won't go if you come with me' would mean the opposite. We need 'unless' (= if you don't).
wrongReasons.whether: 'whether' introduces a choice or a doubt (I don't know whether he will come), not a condition like this.
wrongReasons.as: 'as' gives a reason or a time, not a condition.

questions.text: I won't go ___ you come with me.
